Sarah W: Started an envelope migration sweep against prod-objects.s3 (tenant shards). Hit a bunch of KMS 429s in us-west-2. Paused the job. Anyone seen this at this scale?

Jamal K: Yeah — AWS KMS per-key TPS and account quotas bite at high concurrency. How many rewraps/sec were you doing?

Sarah W: Peak ~900/s, steady ~600/s. Workers=40, each re-encrypts by calling ReEncrypt with CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:alias/redwood-cmk. Logs show RequestLimitExceeded / Throttling.

Leo Infra: AWS defaults are low per-single-CMK. Options: shard keys (regional or per-tenant), introduce client-side token buckets, or request KMS quota bump. Also consider using multi-region replica keys to distribute.

Maria S: From compliance side: we must ensure every rewrap has an audit event: old_key_id, new_key_id, principal, object_key, trace_id, op_ts. Also RBAC — only service role 'envelope-migrator' should have Decrypt/ReEncrypt.

Sarah W: Agreed. Current logs have trace_id but not old_key_id consistently. Will add fields. Quick question: what's equivalent RBAC controls for GCP/Azure?

Natasha P: GCP: IAM on CryptoKey/versions and use a service account with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on specific key versions. Azure: restrict Key Vault access policies / RBAC roles and use Managed Identity. For envelopes, prefer ephemeral DEKs issued by KMS to limit direct KEK traffic.

Jamal K: Practical mitigation plan: 1) checkpointing per-prefix so we can resume after pause, 2) add per-key TPS limiter (token bucket) in the migrator, 3) exponential backoff + jitter on 429s, 4) canary 1% at low rate. Example backoff we use:

```
backoff = ExponentialBackoff(base=200ms, max=10s, jitter=0.2)
for item in queue:
  try:
    rewrap(item)
  except KMSThrottle:
    await backoff.wait()
    requeue(item)
```

Sarah W: Good. Also need run-level observability: metrics for rewrap.items_processed, errors_by_type, kms_429_rate, checkpoint_offset, run_state. SRE needs a dashboard and alerts for increasing 429 rate.

Leo Infra: We'll emit metrics: rewrap.job.<run_id>.processed_count, rewrap.job.<run_id>.kms_429_count, rewrap.job.<run_id>.last_checkpoint_s3. And write a checkpoint file to s3://redwood-migrations/checkpoints/<run_id>.json with worker offsets. We'll set lifecycle to delete after 90d.

Maria S: Compliance note: write immutable audit log copy to the org-audit-bucket (append-only), encrypted with org-level KMS. Redact PII and include only object_id / tenant_id fingerprints.

Sarah W: Plan: implement backoff + per-key token buckets + checkpointing + structured audit events + RBAC tighten. Then do a canary run for 1% of objects in us-west-2 at ~50/s. Tagging @Ops for deploy window.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary run for envelope-migrator: start=2026-04-02T02:00:00Z, run_id=wrp-1782468123-canary, rate=50/s

Ops: I'll coordinate the window and open a support ticket with AWS for temporary KMS quota bump (in case canary shows we need burst).

Sarah W: :thumbsup: I'll update the runbook and push a config PR with token-bucket params and checkpointing. Will follow up with a short post-mortem if any unexpected errors pop up.

encryption-bot: Note: run policy check: ensure 'envelope-migrator' role has least-privilege on KEKs. Found 2 keys with broad access — filing internal ticket #INC-7241.
